name: org.machanism.machai:gw-mcp-server
description: Ghostwriter MCP Server is an executable Java 17 Model Context Protocol server that exposes Ghostwriter project-aware code assistance and Bindex Core metadata retrieval, registration, semantic discovery, and library recommendation workflows to MCP clients. The Maven artifact org.machanism.machai:gw-mcp-server is packaged as a runnable JAR whose entry point is org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer. It supports STDIO by default, HTTP with --port, and streamable HTTP sessions with --session. The server accepts runtime configuration for project directory, advertised server name and version, and properties files. Ghostwriter model-assisted workflows can use the Machai GenAI Client provider layer, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and CodeMie, while local Tools and None providers support tool callbacks or no-op operation. Provider credentials and model selection are configured externally; this module's bundled properties specify Maven-filtered server name and version and gw.properties as the additional configuration file. The project depends on Ghostwriter, Bindex Core, and Machai MCP Server at the project version and targets Java 17.

constructors.description: Creates the MCP server entry-point object. Operational startup is normally performed through the static main method in the assembled executable JAR, which initializes the server runtime and selected transport.

examples.description: Creates the entry-point object. For normal MCP deployment, run the assembled JAR so the runtime initializes and manages the chosen transport.

features.name: main
features.signature: public static void main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.lang.Exception
features.description: Starts the unified Ghostwriter and Bindex MCP tool server. With no port option, the server uses STDIO; -p or --port selects HTTP mode; -s or --session enables streamable HTTP sessions.

examples.description: Starts a named server in STDIO mode for a local MCP client and supplies the current directory as the project context.
Starts a streamable HTTP MCP server on port 45000 for an HTTP-capable MCP client.

features.name: getConfigurator
features.signature: public static org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.PropertiesConfigurator getConfigurator(java.lang.String configFile) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Creates the properties configurator and loads the requested configuration file. A null configFile uses the default MCP configuration and tolerates its absence; an explicitly requested unreadable file causes java.io.IOException.

examples.description: Loads an explicitly named server properties file before startup. Keep provider credentials in a protected configuration file or environment settings rather than source control.

customizations.name: MCP command-line transport and server options
customizations.description: Use -p or --port to select HTTP mode, -s or --session to enable streamable HTTP, -d or --projectDir to provide a project path, -n or --name to set the advertised server name, -v or --version to set the advertised version, -c or --config to select a properties file, and -h or --help for usage information. Without a port, the server uses STDIO.

examples.description: Supplies the project directory and server name, then starts streamable HTTP mode on port 45000.

customizations.name: Ghostwriter AI provider and model configuration
customizations.description: Configure provider selection with the provider-qualified gw.model property, for example OpenAI:gpt-4o-mini or Anthropic:MODEL, and provide the matching provider credentials via secure runtime configuration or environment. OpenAI uses OPENAI_API_KEY and may use OPENAI_BASE_URL; Anthropic uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and may use ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; CodeMie uses GENAI_USERNAME and GENAI_PASSWORD with optional AUTH_URL. The module does not declare a default AI model in its bundled server properties.

examples.description: Selects an OpenAI model for Ghostwriter requests; configure OPENAI_API_KEY outside source control and confirm the model is available to the account.

customizations.name: Additional server configuration file
customizations.description: The bundled mcp-server.properties selects gw.properties as custom_configuration. Use the runtime config option to load server properties and keep secrets outside committed project files.

examples.description: Starts the server with an explicitly selected properties file, which must be readable.

examples.name: Build, configure, and launch a local STDIO MCP server
steps: From the project root, build and install the runnable artifact with mvn clean install -Ppack.
Create a protected gw.properties file to select a provider using gw.model=OpenAI:gpt-4o-mini, and configure the required OPENAI_API_KEY as an environment variable; do not commit credentials.
Configure an MCP client to launch java -jar target/gw-mcp-server-1.4.3.jar --projectDir . --config gw.properties.
Start the MCP client; without a port option, the server communicates over standard input and output.
Use the client's discovered Ghostwriter project workflows or Bindex metadata workflows for the selected project.
examples.description: A practical local-process setup for an IDE or AI assistant using STDIO transport and a configured generative-AI provider.

examples.name: Run a streamable HTTP MCP server
steps: Build the runnable release artifact with mvn clean install -Ppack.
Prepare a protected properties file and provider credentials if model-assisted workflows are required.
Start the server with java -jar target/gw-mcp-server-1.4.3.jar --projectDir . --config gw.properties --port 45000 --session.
Configure an HTTP-capable MCP client to connect to the host and port where the server is listening.
Connect the client and invoke the advertised Ghostwriter or Bindex tools for the target project.
examples.description: Deploys the MCP server over HTTP with streamable sessions enabled.

examples.name: Declare the server artifact in a Maven application
steps: Add the dependency configuration to the application's pom.xml.
Resolve the artifact from Maven Central or make it available in the local Maven repository.
When embedding is intentional, invoke org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer.main from the hosting application; otherwise use the standalone runnable JAR for process isolation.
examples.description: Shows installation through Maven for applications that intentionally embed the server entry point.
